entries.text:
Appendix
Commissioning order
Email this request form, together with the system scheme, to your local Viessmann sales office.
A competent employee must be present when the system is commissioned.
System details:
Requester
System location
Checklist:
= Hydraulic scheme for heating system included
= Heating circuits fully installed and filled
= Electrical installation completed
= Hydraulic lines fully thermally insulated
= Installation completed in full up to refrigerant circuit
= All windows and external doors airtight
= Components for cooling mode fully installed (optional)
= Components for ventilation fully installed (optional)
= Components for photovoltaic system fully installed (optional)
Preferred appointment:
1. Date
Time
2. Date
Time
The work requested from Viessmann will be billed to me/us in accordance with the latest Viessmann pricelist.
Place/date
Signature
Appendix
Final decommissioning and disposal
Viessmann products can be recycled. Components
and substances from the system are not part of ordi-
nary domestic waste.
Complete units and compressors are only to be dis-
posed of via qualified disposal specialists.
Observe the following regulations:
■ Fluorinated greenhouse gas regulation 517/2014/EU
■ Currently applicable regulations and requirements
Isolate the system from the power supply for decom-
missioning. Allow any hot components to cool down.
All components must be disposed of correctly.
Note
Before commencing decommissioning, note the
"Checklist for maintenance work" on page 147.

entries.title: Appendix: final decommissioning and disposal – Final decommissioning and disposal (cont.)
entries.text:
Appendix
Final decommissioning and disposal (cont.)
Decommissioning:
■ Positioning requirements apply only so long as the
outdoor unit is filled with refrigerant: See page 19.
■ Decommissioning may only be carried out by a quali-
fied contractor who is familiar with the equipment
used for refrigerant disposal.
■ For decommissioning and disposal also, work on the
refrigerant circuit may only be carried out by qualified
and certified personnel: See "Safety information".
■ Extract the refrigerant: See chapter "Extracting the
refrigerant" on page 156.
Frost protection:
■ To avoid frost damage, completely remove heating
water from the connection pipes and the condenser
(not required for frost-free storage).
Intermediate storage:
■ Intermediate storage only above ground level with
natural ventilation aperture to the outside
■ Ensure adequate air circulation during intermediate
storage.
■ If the outdoor units dismantled for disposal are not
stored in accordance with the positioning require-
ments, the following steps must be carried out:
■ Extract the refrigerant: See chapter "Extracting the
refrigerant" on page 156.
Transport:
■ Observe transport information: See page 19.
Observe all applicable regulations and requirements.
Note
According to the European regulation on the carriage
of dangerous goods by road (ADR), special regula-
tion 291 for transporting complete units with less
than 12 kg of flammable refrigerant, no special trans-
port requirements need be followed.
■ Transport only in the upright position
■ Use suitable transport brackets.
■ Ensure adequate air circulation during transport.
■ Keep ignition sources away, e.g. flying sparks, smok-
ing, etc.
Appendix

Appendix: final decommissioning and disposal – Final decommissioning and disposal (cont.) Appendix: final decommissioning and disposal – Final decommissioning and disposal (cont.) Appendix
Final decommissioning and disposal (cont.)
Decommissioning:
■ Positioning requirements apply only so long as the
outdoor unit is filled with refrigerant: See page 19.
■ Decommissioning may only be carried out by a quali-
fied contractor who is familiar with the equipment
used for refrigerant disposal.
■ For decommissioning and disposal also, work on the
refrigerant circuit may only be carried out by qualified
and certified personnel: See "Safety information".
■ Extract the refrigerant: See chapter "Extracting the
refrigerant" on page 156.
Frost protection:
■ To avoid frost damage, completely remove heating
water from the connection pipes and the condenser
(not required for frost-free storage).
Intermediate storage:
■ Intermediate storage only above ground level with
natural ventilation aperture to the outside
■ Ensure adequate air circulation during intermediate
storage.
■ If the outdoor units dismantled for disposal are not
stored in accordance with the positioning require-
ments, the following steps must be carried out:
■ Extract the refrigerant: See chapter "Extracting the
refrigerant" on page 156.
Transport:
■ Observe transport information: See page 19.
Observe all applicable regulations and requirements.
Note
According to the European regulation on the carriage
of dangerous goods by road (ADR), special regula-
tion 291 for transporting complete units with less
than 12 kg of flammable refrigerant, no special trans-
port requirements need be followed.
■ Transport only in the upright position
■ Use suitable transport brackets.
■ Ensure adequate air circulation during transport.
■ Keep ignition sources away, e.g. flying sparks, smok-
ing, etc.

Code: F.91
Type: Fault
Affected subsystem: Electrical system
Cause: DIO electronics module communication error
System behaviour:
  - Function of connected components in emergency mode
Measures to take:
  - Check the settings in the commissioning assistant. Adjust settings if required.
  - Check connections to DIO electronics module and connection to HPMU electronics module.
  - Check whether components are wrongly connected.
  - Isolate the system from the power supply. Restart the system.
  - If the fault persists, replace DIO electronics module.

entries.title: FAULT F.867
entries.text:
Code: F.867
Type: Fault
Affected subsystem: Electrical system, Hydraulics, Refrigerant circuit, Vitocal 252-A heating system
Cause: Float air vent valve in the outdoor unit has responded.  Too much air in the secondary circuit during venting  Quick-action air vent valve may be faulty Or  Refrigerant present in the float air vent valve
System behaviour:
  - Heat pump off
Measures to take:
  - Specialist personnel working on a refrigerant circuit with flammable refrigerant are required to have specific qualifications and certification: See "Safety information".
  - Danger Escaping refrigerant can lead to explosions that result in very serious injuries.
  - Observe guidance on measures and steps to take in the event of escaping refrigerant: See "Safety information".
  - If a message appears during venting:
      - Check the quick-action air vent valve. Replace quick-action air vent valve if required.
      - Restart filling programme.
  - If a message appears during operation:
      - Isolate the system from the power supply.
      - Shut off the hydraulic connection between the indoor and outdoor unit.
      - Notify Viessmann Werke Technical Service.
Fix procedure: Vent the heating system (page 86)

entries.title: WARNING A.101
entries.text:
Code: A.101
Type: Warning
Affected subsystem: Refrigerant circuit
Cause: Values for hot gas temperature in relation to hot gas pressure not plausible
System behaviour:
  - Refrigerant circuit operation impaired
Measures to take:
  - Check sensors. Replace both sensors if required.
  - To check the high pressure sensor, measure the voltage at connection X14.1 to X14.3 of the VCMU refrigerant circuit controller (0 to 5 V).
  - To check the hot gas temperature sensor, check resistance value (NTC 10 kΩ) at connection X14.9/X14.10 of the VCMU refrigerant circuit controller.
Measurements:
- Voltage: 0 to 5 V
- Resistance: NTC 10 kΩ
Fix procedure: Check the pressure-sensor output signals (page 121)

entries.title: Commission and start the Vitocal 252-A
entries.text:
Title: Commission and start the Vitocal 252-A
Qualifications required:
  - System installer or a qualified person authorised by the installer.
Purpose: Start the system and complete the commissioning assistant without assuming that every menu item applies to every installation.
Preconditions:
  - Hydraulic lines are connected and checked for leaks; the indoor and outdoor units are hydraulically connected.
  - The system is not yet filled with heating water; electrical components are connected and the indoor unit, instantaneous heating water heater, and outdoor unit have mains supply.
  - Wait at least 30 minutes between installing the outdoor unit and commissioning.
Tools/Equipment:
  - Programming unit or supported commissioning software tool/app.
Steps:
  1. Switch on the outdoor-unit voltage, then the indoor-unit voltage, then start the indoor unit at its ON/OFF switch.
  2. Start the commissioning assistant. If the appliance was already switched on, call up the assistant later through Service > password viservice > Commissioning.
  3. Select the commissioning tool, language, country, date and time, units, system scheme, configured heating/cooling circuits, DHW arrangement, and any connected extensions as applicable.
  4. Confirm whether the outdoor-unit installation conditions are met and whether the refrigerant circuit is ready.
      - Outdoor-unit conditions are met and the refrigerant circuit is ready for operation.
          - Enable the outdoor unit and continue commissioning.
      - Outdoor unit is not ready for operation.
          - Continue with the instantaneous heating water heater only; room cooling is unavailable.
  5. Use the filling assistant to set the system-pressure set value and range, fill the applicable circuits, build system pressure, and run venting; follow the separate cited procedures for these operations.
  6. Complete the applicable extension and system-configuration selections, including power-OFF/Smart Grid, electric booster heater, digital inputs, quieter operation, and screed drying.
  7. Enter commissioning readings in the report from page 164 onwards and the operator's log, if available.
Measurements:
  - Commissioning primary-circuit air temperature differential
  - Commissioning secondary-circuit temperature differential
Acceptance criteria:
  - Commissioning assistant settings are completed for the installed system.
  - Record commissioning readings in the reports and operator's log where available.

entries.title: Fill and top up the heating system
entries.text:
Title: Fill and top up the heating system
Purpose: Fill the applicable consumer circuits through the commissioning assistant using the manual's water-quality, flow-rate, and charge-pressure requirements.
Preconditions:
  - Flush the heating system thoroughly before filling.
  - Do not use antifreeze or a water/glycol mixture in the heating water.
  - Check that the outdoor-unit transport bracket is secured before filling and venting.
Steps:
  1. Use potable-quality fill water with hardness below 3 °dH; treat the water by one of the methods listed in the manual.
  2. Start the menu-guided filling function in the commissioning assistant.
  3. For a 2C indoor unit, fill heating/cooling circuit 2 first: connect fill and drain hoses to that circuit's 3-way ball valves, open both valves, and start the filling process.
  4. Connect fill and drain hoses to the outdoor-unit flow and return 3-way ball valves, open them as shown, and start filling the remaining consumer circuits in turn.
  5. When air bubbles stop coming from the drain hose, advance to the next circuit; after all consumer circuits are filled, end the filling process.
  6. Close the 3-way ball valves and remove the fill and drain hoses.
Measurements:
  - Heating-water filling flow and charge pressure
Resolves: F.74, A.11

entries.text:
Title: Build up system pressure
Purpose: Raise the heating-water pressure after the filling assistant has filled the consumer circuits.
Preconditions:
  - Complete the filling function first; it starts the build-system-pressure function automatically.
Steps:
  1. For an indoor unit with 2 integrated heating/cooling circuits, open the flow to circuit 2 with its 3-way ball valves.
  2. Connect the fill hose to the outdoor-unit flow valve, open the flow and return paths as shown, and slowly admit heating water.
  3. Monitor system pressure on the display and stop the process in the commissioning assistant when the selected required pressure is reached.
  4. Close the outdoor-unit flow valve and remove the fill hose; leave the outdoor-unit flow open as directed.
Measurements:
  - Heating-system pressure
Resolves: F.74, A.11

Title: Vent the heating system
Purpose: Run the commissioning assistant's automatic system venting function.

entries.title: Check expansion-vessel pre-charge and system pressure
entries.text:
Title: Check expansion-vessel pre-charge and system pressure
Purpose: Check vessel suitability and pre-charge on a cold system, then restore heating-water pressure.
Preconditions:
  - Check the pre-charge pressure once a year on a cold system.
  - Drain the system until the pressure indicator shows zero before checking vessel pre-charge.
Steps:
  1. Use the DIN 4807-2 calculation to check vessel capacity against system water volume; add an on-site vessel to the secondary circuit if the installed vessel is insufficient.
  2. On a cold system, drain until the pressure indicator shows zero and measure vessel pre-charge against static system pressure.
  3. If pre-charge is lower than static system pressure, top up with nitrogen at the vessel valve to the specified offset; do not let pre-charge fall below the stated minimum.
  4. Top up with water until the cooled-system charge pressure meets the stated minimum and offset from vessel pre-charge; do not exceed the permissible operating pressure.
Measurements:
  - Expansion-vessel pre-charge pressure
  - Heating-system pressure
Resolves: F.74

  5. For the annual safety-chain test procedure, request the procedure from Viessmann Technical Service; this manual does not provide the test steps.

entries.title: Complete the R290 refrigerant-work safety checklist
entries.text:
Title: Complete the R290 refrigerant-work safety checklist
Qualifications required:
  - Refrigerant-circuit work is restricted to the qualified/certified personnel described in the manual; the manual specifically says this work may only be carried out by Viessmann Technical Services employees.
Purpose: Preserve the manual's required pre-work checks for work on an appliance containing flammable refrigerant.
Preconditions:
  - Only personnel with the qualifications and certification required by the manual may work on the refrigerant circuit.
  - The manual states that refrigerant-circuit work is to be carried out by Viessmann Technical Services employees.
Tools/Equipment:
  - Explosion-proof R290 refrigerant detector.
  - CO2 or powder extinguisher when the listed activities are performed.
  - Adequate ventilation equipment where work is not outdoors.
Steps:
  1. Inform maintenance personnel and people in the vicinity, shut off the area around the outdoor unit, and remove flammable materials and ignition sources.
  2. Before, during and after the work, check the area for escaping R290 with an explosion-proof, suitably sealed detector that does not generate sparks.
  3. Have a CO2 or powder extinguisher to hand when refrigerant is drained or topped up, or when welding/brazing/soldering is carried out.
  4. Provide adequate ventilation before refrigerant-circuit work or brazing/soldering and maintain it throughout the work.
  5. Check the refrigerant system, replacement-part suitability, electrical safety, sealed enclosures, wiring condition, and detector suitability as specified by the checklist.
Measurements:
  - R290 refrigerant-detector response threshold

entries.title: Detect and respond to an R290 refrigerant leak
entries.text:
Title: Detect and respond to an R290 refrigerant leak
Qualifications required:
  - Qualified/certified refrigerant-circuit personnel; the manual states refrigerant-circuit work may only be carried out by Viessmann Technical Services employees.
Preconditions:
  - Complete the R290 refrigerant-work safety checklist.
  - Use only a detector suitable for R290 and without potential ignition sources.
Tools/Equipment:
  - Explosion-proof refrigerant detector suitable for R290; if liquid leak detection is used, it must not contain chlorine.
Steps:
  1. For electronic detection, calibrate the detector in refrigerant-free surroundings for the refrigerant used and set the response threshold below 3 g/a.
  2. If using a liquid leak detector, do not use one containing chlorine.
  3. Check refrigerant-circuit connections for leaks.
  4. If a leak occurs or is suspected, immediately extinguish open flames nearby.
  5. If brazing/soldering is needed to remedy the leak, extract all refrigerant and purge the site with oxygen-free nitrogen before and during the brazing/soldering work.
Measurements:
  - R290 refrigerant-detector response threshold

entries.title: Clean the outdoor-unit heat exchanger (evaporator)
entries.text:
Title: Clean the outdoor-unit heat exchanger (evaporator)
Preconditions:
  - Isolate the outdoor unit from power, safeguard against reconnection, protect the unit against moisture, and do not touch the sharp heat-exchanger edges.
  - Do not use flammable, acidic, solvent-, chloride- or ammonia-containing agents, or abrasive cleaning materials.
Steps:
  1. Clean the rear fins with a long-bristled hand brush, using only mild water-based domestic cleaning agents if needed.
  2. For compressed-air cleaning, open the casing and clean the heat exchanger from the inside out; point the air gun toward the exchanger from the front and from an adequate distance.
  3. Check the aluminium fins for deformation and scratches and repair them with a suitable tool if necessary.
  4. Close the outdoor-unit casing.

entries.title: Inspect and clean the DHW cylinder
entries.text:
Title: Inspect and clean the DHW cylinder
Preconditions:
  - Carry out a visual inspection and, if necessary, cleaning no later than 2 years after commissioning and thereafter as required.
  - Shut off the drinking-water supply and ventilate the DHW pipework by opening a cold and hot water tap.
  - Open DHW/heating-water connections only when the DHW cylinder is depressurised.
  - Keep the air vent valve open when draining the DHW cylinder with a suction pump.
Steps:
  1. Remove thermal insulation and screws, then remove the protective magnesium anode and replace its gasket.
  2. Separate the cylinder from the pipework to prevent contaminants entering it; remove loose deposits with a high-pressure cleaner.
  3. Use only plastic cleaning equipment inside the cylinder. For hard deposits that cannot be removed with a high-pressure cleaner, use a pH-neutral chemical cleaning agent.
  4. Fully drain cleaning-agent residue, flush the cylinder thoroughly, and refit the protective magnesium anode.
  5. Before connecting the anode cables, check resistance across terminals A and B; if it is significantly less than infinity, check whether the anode touches the indirect coil.
Measurements:
  - Protective-anode-to-indirect-coil resistance

entries.title: Extract R290 refrigerant
entries.text:
Title: Extract R290 refrigerant
Qualifications required:
  - Authorised contractor; qualified/certified personnel; the manual says refrigerant-circuit work may only be carried out by Viessmann Technical Services employees.
Preconditions:
  - Complete the R290 refrigerant-work safety checklist.
  - Use only extraction equipment authorised for R290 and refrigerant bottles suitable for R290.
  - Do not mix refrigerants in one recovery bottle.
Tools/Equipment:
  - R290-authorised extraction equipment with current inspection record.
  - R290-compatible labelled recovery bottle with safety valve and shut-off valves.
  - Calibrated scales.
  - Manifold.
  - Oxygen-free nitrogen.
  - Vacuum pump with outlet outside the safety zone.
Steps:
  1. Check the heat-pump condition and service intervals; isolate power and safeguard against reconnection; verify safety requirements; place the refrigerant bottle on calibrated scales.
  2. Connect the bottle to the extraction equipment and connect the equipment through the manifold to a refrigerant-circuit Schrader valve.
  3. Extract refrigerant from all parts of the circuit while monitoring the process; do not fill the bottle above 80% of permitted capacity or exceed its design pressure.
  4. Disconnect and securely close the bottle connection, label the bottle as required, and send it to a suitable disposal/recycling facility.
  5. Purge the circuit with oxygen-free nitrogen for at least 5 minutes, at least twice; do not use air or compressed air. Release the positive pressure and evacuate to the stated absolute pressure.
  6. Carry out the static vacuum test. If vacuum is not maintained, repeat from nitrogen purging.
      - The static vacuum is not maintained.
          - Repeat the sequence from step 5.
      - The static vacuum is maintained.
          - Continue the nitrogen purge and evacuation sequence until the repeat cycle is complete.
  7. Repeat steps 5 and 6 until no refrigerant remains. On the final purge, release positive pressure to atmospheric pressure and do not evacuate further.
      - Refrigerant remains in the circuit.
          - Repeat the nitrogen purge and evacuation sequence.
      - No refrigerant remains in the circuit.
          - On the final purge, release positive pressure to atmospheric pressure and do not evacuate further.
  8. Once evacuation is complete, close the Schrader valves gas-tight while counterholding the valve body and tighten the dust-cap union nut to the stated torque.
  9. Affix the specified dated and signed R290/system-status label to the outdoor unit.
Measurements:
  - R290 extraction vacuum and static vacuum test
  - Outdoor-unit service fastener torques

entries.title: Fill the refrigerant circuit with R290
entries.text:
Title: Fill the refrigerant circuit with R290
Qualifications required:
  - Qualified/certified refrigerant-circuit personnel; the manual says refrigerant-circuit work may only be carried out by Viessmann Technical Services employees.
Preconditions:
  - Complete the R290 refrigerant-work safety checklist.
  - The circuit has been drained and evacuated below 2.7 mbar absolute.
  - After repairs, first perform the pressure-resistance test.
  - Do not use the same fill valve for different refrigerants; position refrigerant bottles vertically.
Tools/Equipment:
  - R290 refrigerant bottle.
  - Calibrated scales.
  - Explosion-proof R290 refrigerant detector.
Steps:
  1. Confirm the safety instructions and earth the refrigerant circuit.
  2. Verify the circuit is drained and evacuated, the absolute pressure before filling is below 2.7 mbar, any replaced parts follow their separate installation instructions, and post-repair pressure testing is complete.
  3. Weigh the refrigerant bottle and fill with R290 through the high-pressure-side 2 Schrader valve (liquid line); do not allow air or oxygen into the circuit and do not exceed the specified charge.
  4. Close the Schrader valves gas-tight while counterholding the valve body and tighten to the stated valve-body and dust-cap torques.
  5. Label the heat pump with refrigerant type and amount, carry out an R290 leak test, and seal the low-pressure Schrader-valve cap.
Measurements:
  - R290 extraction vacuum and static vacuum test
  - R290 circuit pressure-resistance test
  - R290 refrigerant charge weight
  - Outdoor-unit service fastener torques
  - R290 refrigerant-detector response threshold

Qualifications required:
  - Qualified contractor familiar with refrigerant-disposal equipment; refrigerant-circuit work by qualified and certified personnel as stated by the manual.
Preconditions:
  - Decommissioning and refrigerant-circuit work are restricted to qualified/certified personnel described in the manual.
Steps:
  1. Extract the refrigerant using the separate R290 extraction procedure.
  2. To avoid frost damage, completely remove heating water from the connection pipes and condenser unless storage is frost-free.
      - The appliance will not be stored frost-free.
          - Completely remove heating water from the connection pipes and condenser.
